what: The Brev balance, and why CR waits for T1P instead of running beside it
source: Brev low-credit email to luai_abuelsamen@berkeley.edu, 2026-11-02T21:54:43Z. The CLI has no billing command and the Console needs a browser, so this email is how the number was finally obtained.

spend_since.note: 7 boxes brought up between 00:57 and 02:25 UTC, plus b21 which burned ~75 min on a hung apt-get with no clip and was deleted.

decision: CR ($19.18, 6 clips) runs AFTER T1P completes, not in parallel.
why_not_parallel: The low-credit email states that on exhaustion 'your running environments and deployments, along with data, may be stopped or deleted to prevent overages'. Running both leaves about $7 of slack on a night that has already produced seven failed creates and one box (b21) that billed 75 minutes without claiming a clip. Losing T1P near completion costs far more than the wall clock saved, and there is no deadline pressure: T1P finishes ~05:00-06:30 UTC, CR would then finish by ~15:00 UTC, about 31 h before the 2026-11-04 22:00 UTC freeze.
trigger_to_launch_cr: T1P cells all pulled and scored, then re-read the balance from a fresh Brev email or the Console before creating anything.
cr_is_ready: staged at $S/cr_refs (6 clips, 44 files, manifest 44 lines, roles for all six); one command: brev/second_wave.sh --groups CR --go --cap 20
